Compute Match — Environments,
Infrastructure, Delivery and CI
Environments
Environment How applications are delivered
Dev Continuously from protected main
QA Manual promotion of a qualiﬁed Dev snapshot
Staging (STG) Manual promotion of the immutable QA package
( STG_RELEASE_SNAPSHOT_ID )
Production Not enabled from the pipeline until authorized
Infrastructure for each environment is applied by a separate Terraform pipeline. Environment values
live in infrastructure/environments/<env>/ .
Google Cloud infrastructure (Terraform)
Stacks in infrastructure/terraform/stacks/ , applied in order: project-bootstrap  →  environment-
bootstrap  →  computematch  →  platform  →  keycloak .
computematch stack: VPC, GKE Autopilot private cluster, Cloud SQL PostgreSQL,
Memorystore Redis, Secret Manager metadata, Workload Identity, edge and Cloud Armor.
platform stack: namespaces, Kubernetes service accounts, RBAC, NetworkPolicy baselines,
Gateway resources.
keycloak stack: declarative realm and identity-provider conﬁguration.
Terraform owns cloud resources; Helm owns workloads. Runtime secrets live only in Google Secret
Manager.
Helm
Charts in infrastructure/helm/ : workloads backend , frontend , workflow-worker , keycloak ,
superset ; platform db-bootstrap , otel-collector ; library common . Deployment order: db-bootstrap
→  otel-collector →  keycloak →  backend →  worker →  frontend →  superset. Workloads use
SecretSync and Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecars; image digests are pinned in environment values.
Application release train
“Build once, promote digests.” Components: backend, frontend, worker, superset, keycloak.
1. Merge to main  publishes images tagged by commit SHA and mirrors them to Artifact Registry.
2. Dev auto-deploys changed components, runs smoke and functional checks, and records a
snapshot.
3. QA promotes the exact digests and creates the package computematch-release/<snapshot-id>
(manifest plus checksum).
4. Staging consumes that package without rebuilding.
5. Production promotion is not yet enabled.
GitLab CI
Stages: test →  security →  build →  publish →  sync →  plan →  infrastructure →  platform →  deploy →
verify.
Merge requests: path-scoped tests, security scans (secret scan, IaC SAST), image builds
without publishing, read-only Terraform plans.
main : publish images, mirror, Dev release. Infrastructure applies are manual on protected
main  and independent of application releases.
Git workﬂow (CONTRIBUTING.md)
Branch: NCPMS-<number>/<kebab-case-outcome> , for example NCPMS-565/repository-foundation .
One Jira issue per branch; branch from updated main ; no long-lived develop/staging
branches.
Commit: <type>(<scope>): NCPMS-<number> <imperative description> , for example fix(backend): 
NCPMS-855 widen hosting provider name columns . Types: feat, ﬁx, docs, test, refactor, perf, build,
ci, chore, revert. Add !  for breaking changes.
Merge request title: NCPMS-<number>: <Capitalized outcome> . Description sections: Objective,
Changes, Validation, Risk and rollback, Tracking.
Labels: one type:: , one risk::  (low, medium, high), one or more component: ; optional
review:security , review:database , review:platform , breaking-change .
No direct pushes or force pushes to main ; pipelines must pass and discussions be resolved;
fast-forward merges; no whole-MR squash.
Install hooks with pre-commit install  and run pre-commit run --all-files .
